name: Anurag Dikshit
current_role: Philanthropist; founder and trustee of the Kusuma Trust (UK and Gibraltar)
profile: IIT Delhi computer-science graduate who co-founded PartyPoker.com in 1997 and wrote the betting software behind PartyGaming, which listed in London in 2005. He sold his remaining stake by January 2010 and has since focused on the Kusuma Trust, which funds education and children's organisations, mainly in India and Gibraltar.
interesting_fact: The Telegraph reported that in 2010 he and the Sainsbury family were Britain's biggest donors, each giving over GBP 100 million that year; by 2014 about GBP 172.4m had gone to the Kusuma Trust.
deep_cut_fact: Before PartyPoker he worked in the US as a systems analyst at CMC and as a consultant for WebSci and AT&T; he and his wife also set up the Kusuma Gallery at the V&A's Photography Centre. He grew up and went to school (De Nobili School) in Dhanbad.
notes: Low public profile; best route is via Kusuma Trust. Note 2008 US guilty plea (online gambling) and $300m forfeiture - avoid in outreach. Trust does not accept unsolicited funding applications.

name: Hu Zhirong
current_role: Chairman, controlling shareholder and legal representative of Warom Technology (华荣科技, SSE: 603855); chairman of Warom Group
profile: Born 1962, Hu Zhirong controls Warom Technology, a Shanghai-based maker of explosion-proof electrical equipment that also has professional-lighting and new-energy businesses. The group traces its origins to 1987, and the listed company went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in May 2017. Hu holds about 34% of the shares.
interesting_fact: Warom is led by its explosion-proof equipment business, which is used in hazardous oil, gas, chemical and mining settings, and it now also does professional lighting and new energy.
deep_cut_fact: Besides Warom, Hu is listed as executive director of Shanghai Zunrong Yacht Club (上海尊荣游艇俱乐部) and vice-chairman of Fuji Elevator (Sichuan), according to Warom's 2025 annual report.
notes: Low media profile. Best route is the board secretary's office (Song Zongbin, hrzhd@warom.com). Relevant to the energy theme (explosion-proof gear for oil and gas, plus new energy).

name: Xia Chaojia
current_role: Chairman of Hejia Group (禾嘉集团) per an older profile; current status not verified
profile: Sichuan (Chengdu) industrialist who took over a small, run-down neighbourhood factory in 1979 and built it into Hejia Group, which had more than 20 subsidiaries. Its controlled company, Hejia Co. (禾嘉股份), listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 1997. He appeared on Forbes' China mainland rich list for three years in a row.
interesting_fact: In 1998 the group acquired all of Sichuan Feiqiu Group, a large state-owned enterprise nicknamed 'Asia's king of balls' for its football manufacturing.
deep_cut_fact: He started in 1979 by taking over the street factory with 6,000 yuan of borrowed money.
notes: Only found an old profile (qianzhan.com); could not verify his current role or whether he is alive. Hejia Co. was later renamed/restructured, so check current filings.

name: Xue Junteng
current_role: Shareholder of Luolai Lifestyle Technology (罗莱生活, SZSE: 002293); held 7.79% after a March 2019 share sale
profile: Xue Junteng is a major individual shareholder of Luolai Lifestyle, China's large home-textile (bedding) maker, which is controlled by chairman Xue Weicheng. In March 2019 he agreed to sell 25.44 million shares (3.37%) to CA Fabric Investments and kept 58.78 million shares (7.79%). His exact family relationship to the Xue founders was not confirmed in the sources read.
interesting_fact: His 2019 stake sale went to CA Fabric Investments, bringing in an outside strategic investor at Luolai.
notes: No biography found. Listed with Xue Weibin as wealth-sharer, but no source found linking the two. Appears to be a passive shareholder, not an executive. Route via Luolai's IR office if needed.

name: Gong Mingjie
current_role: Chairman and legal representative of Longda Foodstuff Group (龙大食品集团), Laiyang, Shandong (as of 2020 filing)
profile: Gong Mingjie chairs Longda Foodstuff Group, the Laiyang, Shandong food-processing group that was the controlling shareholder of the listed meat company Longda Meat (later Longda Meishi, SZSE: 002726). As of 2020 he and Gong Xuebin together held 64.17% of the group. The group sold blocks of its stake in the listed company in 2019-2020.
interesting_fact: Longda Group is based in Longwangzhuang subdistrict of Laiyang, a Shandong city known for food processing.
notes: The 2020 filing lists Longda Group's phone, but no email/site was found. The listed company is now 'ST Longda' (2026). His current role was not verified after 2020.
